Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Togo's e-ID (ANID/MOSIP) system is partially deployed. After Law No.2020-009 and a 2023 contract award to IDEMIA/Atos, mass biometric enrollment began rolling out region by region (Gulf, Agoè-Nyivé, Savanes, and Maritime from Nov 2025). The system is not yet nationwide/fully deployed as enrollment is still progressing prefecture by prefecture.

revision_notes: All three original sources were fetched and are live and on-topic; they support the narrative in Comments. Fresher evidence (Biometric Update and Togo First, both April 2026, drawing on the government's H2-2025 reform monitoring report) shows over 6 million NIUs/biometric cards issued by end-December 2025 (roughly two-thirds of the ~9.6m population), with phased regional enrollment still ongoing into 2026 (e.g. Plateaux Zone 1, March-April 2026) and a stated 2026 target of 8m+ credentials. This confirms the system is operational but still rolling out region-by-region rather than nationwide and open to new registrations everywhere simultaneously, so Value Code 4 (Partially deployed) is confirmed, not upgraded to 5.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: In July 2021, ARCEP launched a SIM card registration campaign requiring a national identity card or passport with biometric and demographic data collection (per CIPESA 2022). SIM registration is mandatory in Togo, requiring government-issued ID documents. This makes the national ID mandatory for SIM registration per ARCEP requirements.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The single original CIPESA source was fetched, is live and relevant, and its claim is corroborated. A government decree of 26 December 2024 (reported by Telecompaper, Techs.tg and CIOMAG, Jan 2025) reinforces and formalises mandatory prior identification of all electronic communications subscribers, banning pre-activated/unidentified SIM sales, building on a 2021 ARCEP measure requiring an ID card, passport, driving licence or voter's card. Proof of identity (traditionally a national ID document, with the new e-ID/NIU credential increasingly used) remains mandatory to obtain mobile service, so Value Code 3 (Mandatory) is confirmed with two additional independent, dated sources rather than resting on one.
